title: Short sums of certain arithmetic functions (Nair–Tenenbaum)
abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Nair and Tenenbaum's uniform upper bounds for short sums of nonnegative arithmetic functions evaluated at integer polynomial values. Theorem 1 retains the coefficient-independent height threshold and the restricted-discriminant dependence of the bound. Theorem 2 gives a greatest-prime-factor bound with a strict exponential gain for arbitrary nonconstant irreducible integer polynomials, including those with fixed prime divisors. Theorem 3 treats prime arguments with the explicit constant-term correction. The development also proves the ten corollaries on progressions, Hooley moments, smooth values, shifted primes, dyadic averages, and Goldbach representations, and Lemma 2 for general class-M weights. Corollary 6 has an explicit nonconstancy condition; the printed Lemma 1 has a checked counterexample and the required replacements are proved.
